reading.passage: So this is it — senior high school at last! In the morning, Han Jing felt a little anxious because she is not very outgoing. She wanted to make a good first impression, and she kept wondering whether she would make any friends. Her first maths class was difficult, but the teacher was kind and friendly. He told the class a funny story, and everyone laughed. Han Jing found most of her classmates and teachers friendly and helpful. In the afternoon, they had a chemistry class in the science lab. The lab was new and the layout was great, but the boy next to her talked the whole time, so she could not concentrate on the experiment. By the evening, Han Jing felt much better. She did not feel awkward or frightened at all. She still missed her friends from junior high school, but she believed she would make new friends here, and that there was a lot to explore at senior high school. She felt much more confident than she did in the morning, and she thought that tomorrow would be a great day.

reading.passage: Hi! My name is Adam and I'm a freshman at senior high school. Going from junior high school to senior high school is a really big challenge, and my first week was a little confusing. First, I had to think carefully about which courses I wanted to take. The school adviser helped me choose the suitable ones: maths, English, chemistry, world history, and Chinese. I know that Chinese is a very difficult language, but I hope to be fluent when I graduate. My adviser also recommended that I should sign up for advanced literature, because I like English and I'm good at it. I had to choose extra-curricular activities, too. I tried to join the school football team, but the coach told me that I didn't play well enough. Obviously, I was unhappy, but I won't quit. I'll find a way to improve on my own so that I can make the team next year. Instead, I joined a volunteer club. Every Wednesday, we hand out food to homeless people in the community. I know I'll have to study harder and get used to being responsible for a lot more. Still, I'm happy to be here, and I'll be well prepared for whatever comes in the future.
reading.passageCn: 嗨!我叫 Adam,是一名高一新生。从初中升入高中是个很大的挑战,开学第一周有点令人困惑。首先,我得仔细考虑选哪些课程,学业顾问帮我选了合适的:数学、英语、化学、世界历史和语文。我知道汉语很难,但希望毕业时能说得流利。顾问还建议我报名高级文学,因为我喜欢英语也擅长它。我也得选课外活动:我想加入校足球队,但教练说我踢得不够好。我虽然不开心,但我不会放弃,会自己想办法提高,争取明年进队。于是我改加入了志愿者社团,每周三给社区里无家可归的人发放食物。我知道以后要更努力学习,承担更多责任。不过我很高兴来到这里,会为将来做好准备。

finalReading.passage: When the bridge in his town was about to be taken down, old Mr Lin spent months photographing every stone and writing down the stories people told about it. He sold the stones to a museum.

The memory of a place can survive even after it is gone.

Museums should not teach young people.

lines.cn: 它们因象牙被捕猎,栖息地也越来越小。

reading.passage: Lily was too shy to sing in front of others, so she joined a virtual choir online. Singing alone in her room, she added her quiet voice to hundreds of others. When she finally heard the finished song, she felt proud to be part of something so big.
reading.passageCn: 莉莉太害羞,不敢当众唱歌,于是她在网上加入了一个虚拟合唱团。她独自在房间里歌唱,把自己轻轻的歌声加入到数百人之中。当她最终听到合成的歌曲时,她为自己成为这么宏大事物的一部分而感到自豪。

finalReading.passage: When Max felt nervous before his first concert, his teacher handed him a small drum and told him to play whatever he felt. To his surprise, the simple beat calmed his shaking hands and helped him forget the crowd. By the end of the night, he was smiling, proud that a few honest sounds had carried him through.

questions.q: How did Max feel before the concert?
options: Calm and confident.
Nervous, with shaking hands.
Bored and sleepy.
Angry at his teacher.
questions.explanation: 原文 'felt nervous… calmed his shaking hands' 的转述,说明他演出前紧张。

questions.q: What helped Max get through the concert?
options: Leaving the stage early.
A long speech from the teacher.
Playing a simple beat on the drum.
Listening to the crowd cheer.
questions.explanation: 原文 'the simple beat calmed his shaking hands… carried him through' 的转述(覆盖短文后半)。
